title: Etale scheme-chart criterion for geometric Tor independence of algebraic spaces
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $F,G,H$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with morphisms $F\to H$ and $G\to H$. Their geometric local rings are stalks of the small etale structure sheaves. Say that $F$ and $G$ are geometrically Tor independent over $H$ if for every pair $\bar f:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to F$, $\bar g:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to G$ over the same $\bar h:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to H$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, $\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathcal O_{H,\bar h}}_i(\mathcal O_{F,\bar f},\mathcal O_{G,\bar g})=0$ for all $i>0$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Let $W\to H$ be a surjective etale morphism from a scheme, and let $U\to F\times_HW$ and $V\to G\times_HW$ be surjective etale morphisms from schemes [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Then $F$ and $G$ are geometrically Tor independent over $H$ if and only if for every pair of ordinary points $u\in U$, $v\in V$ with common image $w\in W$, one has
$$\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathcal O_{W,w}}_i(\mathcal O_{U,u},\mathcal O_{V,v})=0\qquad(i>0).$$
This holds for every such choice of the three scheme atlases. In particular, for schemes $F,G,H$, geometric Tor independence is equivalent to this ordinary local-ring condition on $F,G,H$ themselves. No flatness, quasi-compactness, separation or finiteness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 08IP (definition-tor-independent) and 08IQ (lemma-tor-independent), equivalence (1) and (4), and the scheme comparison in its proof.

proof.text:
Use the following specialization of the cited flat-ring-diagram cohomology comparison: for compatible rings $R,A,B,R_1,A_1,B_1$ satisfying its three flatness assumptions, put $D=A\otimes_RB$, $D_1=A_1\otimes_{R_1}B_1$. Taking $M=A[0]$ and cohomological degree $-i$ gives
$$\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(A,B)\otimes_DD_1\cong\operatorname{Tor}_i^{R_1}(A_1,B_1).$$
Indeed $A\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_1=A_1[0]$; a projective resolution in homological degrees $i\ge0$, placed in cohomological degrees $-i$, identifies the two displayed cohomology groups with precisely these Tor groups. This also supplies their commuting factor actions and the induced $D\to D_1$ map; those actions are part of the cited comparison's statement.

source.place: Tag 08IQ (lemma-tor-independent), displayed Tor comparison; more-algebra.tex Tag 0DJD (lemma-lemma-tor-independent-flat-compare), specialized to M=A[0].

proof.text: First work with schemes $X,Y,Z$ and maps $X\to Z\leftarrow Y$. Fix compatible geometric points over $x,y,z$, and write $R=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ and $\widetilde R,\widetilde A,\widetilde B$ for their geometric local rings. The chart-stalk identification identifies these with compatible strict henselizations. The ordinary local homomorphisms $R\to A,B$ give local strict-henselization maps, and strict-local refinement makes $A\otimes_R\widetilde R\to\widetilde A$ and $B\otimes_R\widetilde R\to\widetilde B$ flat. Also $R\to\widetilde R$ is faithfully flat. Thus step 1 applies. If every ordinary local Tor group in the statement is zero, the resulting geometric Tor groups are zero. This proves the ordinary-to-geometric direction for schemes without any Noetherian assumption.

source.place: Tag 08IQ (lemma-tor-independent), scheme comparison, forward implication; algebra.tex Tag 08HV (lemma-strictly-henselian-functorial-improve); more-algebra.tex Tag 07QM (lemma-dumb-properties-henselization).

proof.text:
For the converse assume geometric Tor independence for schemes. Restrict to affine open neighbourhoods $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}B$ mapping into $Z_0=\operatorname{Spec}R$; their geometric local rings agree with those of $X,Y,Z$ by the etale chart-stalk isomorphisms. Fix $i>0$ and set $D=A\otimes_RB$, $N=\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(A,B)$ with its $D$-action from step 1. For $s\in\operatorname{Spec}D$ write $p,q,r$ for its contractions to $A,B,R$, and put $E=A_p\otimes_{R_r}B_q$, $L=\operatorname{Tor}_i^{R_r}(A_p,B_q)$. The maps $R\to R_r$, $A\otimes_RR_r\to A_p$, and $B\otimes_RR_r\to B_q$ are localizations: on fractions the latter maps invert the remaining elements outside $p,q$. Hence they are flat. Step 1 gives $N\otimes_DE\cong L$. Every denominator used in $D\to E$ lies outside $s$, so the map extends to $E\to D_s$; tensoring the displayed isomorphism with $D_s$ yields
$$N_s\cong L\otimes_ED_s.$$
The localization and tensor identifications are the fraction maps $(a/u)\otimes(b/v)\mapsto(a\otimes b)/(u\otimes v)$.

source.place: Tag 08IQ (lemma-tor-independent), affine converse; more-algebra.tex Tags 08HW (lemma-tor-independent-flat), 08HX (lemma-tor-independent), localization formula in its proof.

proof.text:
Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(s)$. The affine fibre-product identification gives a geometric point $\bar s$ of $X_0\times_{Z_0}Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}D$ and its compatible images $\bar x,\bar y,\bar z$. Put $C=(D_s)^{\mathrm{sh}}$, $T=\widetilde A\otimes_{\widetilde R}\widetilde B$, where tildes are the strict henselizations of $A_p,B_q,R_r$ for these points. Functoriality of strict henselization for the projections gives compatible maps $\widetilde A,\widetilde B\to C$. They agree on $\widetilde R$: their composites are the local map for the same morphism and the same residue-field embedding, hence equal by uniqueness. The tensor universal property gives $T\to C$, compatible with $E\to D_s\to C$. Step 2's application of step 1 gives $L\otimes_ET\cong\operatorname{Tor}_i^{\widetilde R}(\widetilde A,\widetilde B)=0$. Therefore
$$N_s\otimes_{D_s}C\cong L\otimes_EC\cong(L\otimes_ET)\otimes_TC=0.$$
Faithful flatness of $D_s\to C$ implies $N_s=0$: apply the defining reflection of exactness to $0\to N_s\to0$. This holds for every $s$. Apply local detection of bijectivity to $0\to N$ at all maximal ideals of $D$ to conclude $N=0$.

source.place: Tag 08IQ (lemma-tor-independent), affine converse, detecting the localized Tor groups; schemes.tex Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); more-algebra.tex Tag 07QM (lemma-dumb-properties-henselization).

proof.text: For any $x\in X$, $y\in Y$ with common image $z$, choose affine neighbourhoods $X_0,Y_0$ inside the inverse images of an affine neighbourhood $Z_0$ of $z$. This only uses that affine opens form a basis of a scheme. With rings $A,B,R$ as in step 3, the previous step gives $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(A,B)=0$ for every $i>0$. Apply step 1 to the localization diagram $R\to R_r$, $A\to A_p$, $B\to B_q$, whose flatness was checked in step 3. It follows that $\operatorname{Tor}_i^{R_r}(A_p,B_q)=0$. The ordinary affine-open stalk-localization isomorphisms identify these rings and their maps with $\mathcal O_{Z,z},\mathcal O_{X,x},\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. This proves the converse for schemes. No intersections of affine opens are assumed affine.

source.place: Tag 08IQ (lemma-tor-independent), conclusion of the affine converse; more-algebra.tex Tag 08HX (lemma-tor-independent), implication (1) to (2).

proof.text: Now use the atlases of the statement. Base change and composition of representable etale maps show that $U\to F$ and $V\to G$ are etale, as is $W\to H$. For compatible geometric points $\bar u,\bar v$ over $\bar w$, their three geometric local rings and the maps between them are identified with those on $F,G,H$ by the etale chart-stalk isomorphisms. Thus geometric Tor independence on $F,G,H$ implies it on $U,V,W$. Conversely fix any $\bar f,\bar g$ over $\bar h$, all defined over one algebraically closed field $\Omega$. Surjectivity chooses a point of $W$ over the image of $\bar h$, and the specified-point lifting lemma lifts $\bar h$ to $\bar w:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to W$. The fibre-product universal property gives points $(\bar f,\bar w)$ and $(\bar g,\bar w)$ of $F\times_HW$ and $G\times_HW$. Use surjectivity and the same lifting lemma to lift them to $\bar u$ and $\bar v$. All lifts use the original $\Omega$ and have the same image $\bar w$. The same three stalk isomorphisms identify their Tor groups with those of the original triple. Hence geometric Tor independence on $U,V,W$ implies it on $F,G,H$.

source.place: Tag 08IQ (lemma-tor-independent), first two paragraphs, using spaces-properties.tex Tags 04KF (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring), 05VN (lemma-geometric-lift-to-usual).

proof.text: Step 6 identifies geometric Tor independence on $F,G,H$ with geometric Tor independence on the schemes $U,V,W$. Steps 2--5 identify the latter with exactly the stated ordinary local-ring condition on every pair $u,v$ over $w$. The atlases were arbitrary, proving independence of their choice. For schemes take all three atlas maps to be identities, giving the last assertion. The proof nowhere requires the original morphisms to be flat, or the spaces to satisfy any quasi-compactness, separation or finiteness condition.
